Why test here instead of Windows' test page?

Windows' built-in joy.cpl/Test USB game controllers page only displays the first controller in a multi-pad setup, even when the other pads work fine in games. This page shows each pad side by side, with its own live visual and a per-controller activity check — so a pad that stops reporting input is easy to spot.
Connect a controller via USB or Bluetooth (Windows, Mac, Linux, or ChromeOS).
Press any button or move a stick — the matching control lights up and its value updates live.
If nothing detects at first, press a button once; some browsers only wake a pad after its first input.
With multiple pads connected, each one gets its own card — look for the one marked No input yet.
This page is a handy companion for PocketPad: verify the controller before you blame the game.
Bluetooth HID: run PocketPad on your phone, tap Prepare for pairing, pair from your PC, then play a few buttons here.
Wi‑Fi + Companion: with PocketPad connected over Wi‑Fi on Windows, each phone appears here as its own virtual controller — even if the system test dialog would only show the first one.
If a card stays on No input yet while the pad works elsewhere, it is usually a stale virtual controller — reconnect the pad in Companion or re-pair Bluetooth, then press Reset checks.
Any controller the browser can see — Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, generic USB HID pads, keyboard-navigable remotes exposing a gamepad, and virtual pads from tools such as Companion or JoyToKey.
Works with any number of connected gamepads at the same time.

Shows the browser-standard standard layout for Xbox-style pads; on PlayStation pads the stick positions map by position, so glyphs (✕/△/◯/▢) may look rearranged — the raw button numbers below each pad are the ground truth.
Also test vibration when the pad exposes a rumble actuator.
